descriptionChirho: Qal intransitive sense: to be strong, stout, bold, or courageous; to prevail or prove stronger than another. Used especially in exhortations to military and spiritual courage (Deut 31:6-7, Josh 1:6-9, 1 Chr 22:13, 28:20), and in narrative to describe prevailing in conflict (2 Sam 22:18, 2 Chr 13:18). The multilingual glosses consistently render 'be courageous/strong' (arb: تَشَجَّعْ, kor: 담대하라, spa: valiente). Includes Qal imperative, imperfect, and perfect forms.

Piel causative sense: to strengthen, make firm, or encourage another person or thing. The subject actively imparts strength to the object. Used of God strengthening his people (Ps 89:21, Isa 41:10, 44:14), of humans encouraging one another (Deut 3:28, Job 4:4, 16:5), and of making structures firm (Prov 8:28). Glosses show causative semantics across languages (eng: strengthen, fortify; spa: fortalecer; kor: 강하게 하다; hin: दृढ़ करना). Distinct from the intransitive Qal 'be strong.'

Piel with negative moral nuance: to harden the heart or spirit, making someone stubborn, obstinate, or intractable. Semantically specialized from the general Piel 'strengthen' by applying to the will or disposition in a context of resistance to God or to right action. Key passages include Deut 2:30 (God hardened Sihon's spirit), Deut 15:7 (do not harden your heart against the poor), and 2 Chr 36:13 (Zedekiah hardened his neck). Arabic glosses use قَسَّى 'make hard,' distinguishing this from the positive 'strengthen.'

Hiphil causative-jussive sense: to cause someone to take courage or to let one's heart be strengthened. Attested in Ps 27:14 and 31:24 as exhortations (וְיַאֲמֵץ לִבֶּךָ, 'let your heart take courage'). Functionally overlaps with the Piel but is distinctly Hiphil in morphology and tends toward enabling an internal state of courage rather than externally strengthening. Korean renders 담대하게 하라 'cause to be bold,' Arabic وَيَتَشَجَّعْ 'and let him be courageous.'

Hitpael reflexive sense: to strengthen oneself, exert oneself with resolve, or show firm determination. Used of Ruth's resolve to go with Naomi (Ruth 1:18, מִתְאַמֶּצֶת 'she was determined'), and of Rehoboam who strengthened himself in his kingdom (1 Kgs 12:18, 2 Chr 13:7). The reflexive-intensive force distinguishes it from the simple Qal (be strong) and the causative Piel (make strong). Glosses include 'strengthened himself,' 'se esforzó,' '힘썼다.'

Hitpael idiomatic extension: to exert oneself to the point of urgent haste or pressing forward. In 2 Chr 10:18, Rehoboam הִתְאַמֵּץ to mount his chariot in haste to flee. The semantic development from 'strengthen oneself' to 'make haste' reflects the idea of summoning all one's strength for urgent action. English glosses render 'made haste,' Arabic أَسْرَعَ 'hastened,' Spanish 'se apresuró.' A contextually specialized use of the Hitpael reflexive.
